Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week — procurement asked me to confirm a couple of items before we proceed to signature. Attached is the latest Order Form (PDF) and a short matrix from our privacy team showing required processor roles.

Two specific asks from our side:
- Can Redwood confirm which sub-processors will be involved for embeddings storage and any third-party vector search? We need names + locations for transfer impact assessment.
- Your proposed DPA allocates "subprocessor" responsibilities to Redwood; our legal wants a clearer split in Table A (controller/processor mapping) and a model clause for SCCs.

Could you share a version with tracked changes and a short note on transfer risk (esp. US cross-border reliance)? Procurement would like evidence of your SCCs mapping and any supplementary Transfer Impact Assessment you maintain.

Elena — thanks for sending. Looping in Dev (product infra) and Rishi (privacy/legal) to align on the mapping. Quick answers up front:

- Sub-processors: We use VectorStore Inc. (US) for optional managed vector index and CloudLogs Ltd. (EU) for audit log retention. We can provide a subprocessor list and locations under NDA/DocuSign if that helps procurement.
- Table A mapping: we agree it needs to be explicit. Drafting tracked-change version that separates "processing activities" (Redwood inference runtime, KV cache) vs "sub-processing" (vector store + logs).

Action items:
1) Dev to produce a one-page transfer-impact note for the two subprocessors.
2) Legal to propose revised Table A and SCCs addendum language.
3) I'll circulate redlines for your team to review by EOD tomorrow.

— Mina
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference

Mina / Elena — attached are the proposed redlines (DPA v3) and an export impact matrix. Highlights and rationale:

- Table A: I split the processing activities into two columns: (i) core inference (Redwood as processor) and (ii) auxiliary storage/indexing (sub-processors named). This should satisfy FinServ's requirement for explicit role allocation.
- SCCs: I inserted modular SCC exhibits that reference the EU Commission standard clauses and included a short fallback where the parties agree to adopt an equivalent UK addendum if needed.
- Transfer Impact: Appendix B is a concise summary of assessed risks for VectorStore Inc. (US) and CloudLogs Ltd. (EU). For VectorStore, we note reliance on SCCs + documented technical controls (encryption at rest, restricted access). For CloudLogs (EU) impact is minimal.
- Retention / access controls: tightened in Section 4.2 — retention windows for debug logs reduced and explicit roles for deletion requests.

Please review the redlines and the export_impact_matrix.xlsx; I flagged three clauses for commercial review that may affect order form fees: encryption key management, audit log retention, and emergency data access for support.

Attachments: redlines_finserv_dpa_v3.docx, export_impact_matrix.xlsx

Thanks — Rishi
Lead Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — I've reviewed the redlines and the transfer matrix with our privacy counsel (Matt copied). A few closing notes:

- The Table A split looks good — that should clear our procurement checklist.
- We need a confirmation statement that Redwood will provide advance notice of any new EU->US subprocessor transfers and a 30-day objection window. Can Redwood accept notice + objection procedure in Section 6?
- For VectorStore (US) we want either: (a) committed encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys (at additional fee), or (b) contractual assurance of SSE with documented access logs and yearly SOC2 Type II evidence. Please confirm which option Redwood will commit to in the Order Form.

If you can confirm the notice/objection language and the VectorStore key option by Monday EOD, procurement will finalize the order form and we can route for signature.

Best,
Elena
